newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian AIDS awareness high but resistance growing.
newsitem.headline: Belgian AIDS awareness high but resistance growing.

text.p: Awareness of the dangers of contracting AIDS is very high in Belgium, but campaigns have had little effect on sexual behaviour and it has the lowest per capita usage of condoms in Europe, researchers said on Thursday.
"Initially we believed that awareness alone would be enough to produce a change in behaviour," psychologist Ann Buysse of Ghent University told a news conference.
"But we have become increasingly aware that there is a gulf between knowledge and its translation into acts," she added.

Joelle Defourny from the Liege University AIDS reference centre said their research showed there was a growing resistance to campaigns to make people aware of the risks of contracting Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome.
"AIDS awareness is very strong, but the fear is fading," she said. "We believe that prevention and its related messages remain necessary, but they must be adapted to their target audience."
Francoise Uurling, a doctor at the Liege AIDS centre, said the problem was a combination of ignorance and attitude.

"People, especially the young, are not always sure when they should use a condom," she said, adding that the latex preservative remained -- apart from abstinence -- the surest way of preventing the passing of sexually-transmitted diseases.
All three agreed that women were far more aware than men of the risks of infection from unprotected sex and therefore much more willing to take the initiative in using a condom.

Valerie Carbonelle, marketing manager of the London Rubber Company's Durex condom brand, said the most frequent reason for people having unprotected sex -- both inside and outside a relationship -- was that they found using a condom unpleasant.
She said Belgium had the lowest usage of condoms per head per year of the sexually active population of any country in Europe at an average of just three per year.
According the public health ministry 9,606 people have been diagnosed as having HIV, the precursor to AIDS, in Belgium since the disease was first identified in the mid-1980s.
Between 1987 and 1993, 71 HIV infections were diagnosed each month. This dropped to 64 per month in 1994 and is still declining.
One-third of the total number of infections have come from heterosexual contacts, and one-fifth from homosexual or bisexual contacts. Twice as many men as women have the disease.
During the same period 2,231 people have been diagnosed with full-blown AIDS. As with HIV the numbers diagnosed have shown a tendency to decline since 1994.

Figures distributed by the health ministry but attributed to the French-based European Centre for the Surveillance of the AIDS Epidemic show that 167,021 people in the European Union have so far been diagnosed as having AIDS.
On average three-quarters of these cases have come from either homosexual or bisexual contacts or intravenous drug users, with 14 percent from heterosexual contacts.

"We have get more people using condoms. We have to make them more appealing," said Durex quality control manager Nick White. "That is why we have introduced coloured and flavoured condoms. They are not novelties. They are serious fun."
